newsitem.title: USA: Black & Decker reports drop in profits.
newsitem.headline: Black & Decker reports drop in profits.

text.p: Black & Decker Corp. Friday reported a 25 percent drop in fourth-quarter profits despite record sales, attributing the decline partly to lower profitability in its power tools and accessories.
But the Towson, Md.-based company reported a 2.5 percent increase in profits for the year.
Black & Decker reported net income of $90.6 million, or 94 cents a share for the quarter, compared with $120 million, or $1.26 a share in the 1995 period.
Sales hit $1.45 billion vs. $1.44 billion a year ago.
The results were in line with Wall Street analysts' expectations.
However, Black & Decker Chairman Nolan Archibald cautioned in a statement that earnings growth in 1997 was likely to slow due to an increased tax rate.
The company's stock dropped 62.5 cents to $33.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
For the year, the company reported profits of $229.6 million, or $2.38 per share, compared with earnings of $224 million, or $2.37 a share, in 1995.
Black & Decker rang up $4.91 billion in sales, a 3 percent rise from the $4.77 billion recorded in 1995.

"While the combined power tools and accessories business achieved record sales (in 1996), profitability declined, largely because of manufacturing start-up costs, aggressive inventory reduction, higher transportation costs and selective price reductions," Archibald said in the statement.
The company's household products unit reported a decline in sales and profits compared to "a very strong 1995," largely due to a cut in prices for its SnakeLight flexible flashlights.

"Lower profitability in power tools and accessories and in household products was more than offset by the excellent performance of all of our other businesses," including security hardware, plumbing products and recreational products, Archibald said.
